title: What are Dependency Injection and its lifetimes in .NET?
description: Understand DI patterns and service lifetimes.

data.text: **Question:** What are Dependency Injection and its lifetimes in .NET?

Dependency Injection (DI) is a design pattern that implements Inversion of Control. .NET has three main service lifetimes: Transient (created each time), Scoped (once per request), and Singleton (once per application).

**Transient:**
- A new instance is created every time it is requested
- Best for lightweight stateless services
- Example: ILogger, IMailSender

**Scoped:**
- One instance per scope (typically one per HTTP request)
- Best for services that maintain state during a request
- Example: DbContext in ASP.NET Core

**Singleton:**
- One instance for the entire application lifetime
- Must be thread-safe
- Example: IMemoryCache, configuration services
